field.value: <<bb>>Performance Test <</bb>> <<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>>Place Trebor pump on Trebor Pump Test Station (TPTS) grate. Connect the two Teflon pump 3/4" adapter ball valve fittings to Trebor pump ports marked "IN" and "OUT". Use the Trebor AM082 thin Teflon gaskets washers to seal the adapter ends to the pump. Connect 3/8" pnuematic air supply lines to Trebor pump station base ports "SUPLY A" and "SUPLY B". Connect TPST pump station backpressure gauge 1/4" tubing "PRES" hose to upper pump "OUT" port adapter fitting. Slide in the 3/8" U shaped plastic centering fixture on the grate to center the Trebor pump base to the test station.

field.value: <<bb>>Performance Test <</bb>> <<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>>Rinse and Test the Trebor Pump. Not all pumps will run. For the tested pumps record the pumps pressure on the performance data test sheet. For other pumps not known to be broken - will cycle tested. <<nl/>><<nl/>>Using the PUMP SUPPLY Air Regulator knob, increase the air supply to 20 psi by adjusting the knob and reading the right hand gauge marked PUMP PRES. Turn the "PUMP ENABLE" switch ON and adjust the speed to 107 strokes per minute. The "PUMP SPEED" knob can be turned to the predetermined panel mark or verified using a frequency counter. 107 strokes per minute is approx. 1.78 Hz. The pump should start to run and pump water from the "IN" port to the "OUT" port. You should observe water flowing in the transparent input and output pipes. Increase the air pressure to 40 psi. Check for leaks and noises. After 5 minutes of running the pump at 60 psi - record the backpressure reading obtained by the pump. Record the center gauge back pressure "PUMP OUTPUT" pressure gauge. Using the PUMP SUPPLY Air Regulator knob, increase the air supply to 20 psi by adjusting the knob and reading the right hand gauge marked PUMP PRES. Turn the "PUMP ENABLE" switch ON and adjust the speed to 107 strokes per minute. The technician will observe the pump running for 90 seconds everytime the pressure is increased.

After 5 minutes of running the pump at 60 psi - record the backpressure reading obtained by the pump. Record the center gauge back pressure "PUMP OUTPUT" pressure gauge. Knowing the pumps backpressure reading before pump disassembly and cleaning will assist Intel IMR to choose the correct rebuild kit.

field.value: <<bb>>Performance Test <</bb>> <<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>>Perform Purge and Vacuum Test. Disconnect pump IN ball valve adapter so it will not pump water into the pump. Connect the air purge adapter fitting to the pump "IN" pump fitting. Connect the clear 3/8" tubing marked "PURGE" to the IN adapter pump male connector fitting. Connect the purge drain output adapter fitting to the OUT port of the pump. Start the purge presure at 20 psi by adjusting setting the "PUMP SUPPLY" regulator knob and reading the pressure on the "PUMP PRES" right hand gauge. Turn on the purge air to the pump by opening the panel righthand "PURGE" Valve. Start the pump by turning on the "PUMP ENABLE" switch. The pump will pump and will force water into the drain line. <<nl/>><<nl/>> Cycle the pump for 2 minutes until no moisture is seen in the drain line. Increase the purge pressure to 40 psi and cycle the pump sparingly, no more that 90 seconds. The pump shall not be ran dry for long periods. To assit in complete water purge turn off the "PUMP ENABLE" oscillator and turn ON the manual purge switch. The switch UP position turns ON the air to "SUPY A" port, the switch DOWN position turns ON the air to "SUPY B" port. Lift the pump up and tilt the pump side to side to assist in manual water purge removal. The manual purge enables the pump to be purged for long periods until dry without risking cycling the pump. The pump is considered dry when no water or mist vapors are seen at the OUT port when the pump is moved side to side while purging.<<nl/>><<nl/>> <<nl/>><<nl/>>Disconnect the purge air supply and drain lines from the pump. Remove the top pump adapter fitting that attaches to the OUT port of the pump. Remove the 3/8 tubing male connector from the lower fitting that connects to the IN fitting. Install a 1/4" tubing male connector and connect the 1/4" hose marked "VAC" to the lower fitting adapter IN port of the pump. Enable the pump vacuum to be measured by turning on the "VAC ENABLE" valve. Adjust the pump pressure to 40 psi and cycle the pump. Wa

If fittings are too tight use an 15/16" open end wrench or an adjustable wrench to loosen the transfer tube plastic black fittings. The tranfer tube nipples are PFA Teflon and the black nuts and ferrules are polyproplene. Loosen all (4) nuts evenly, then separate the black pump base from the main Trebor pump body. Each transfer tube assembly will have a split ferrule (back) and a ring ferrule (front). Do not loose them, and set aside for cleaning.<<nl/>><<nl/>>Using a clean 1/4 SST Allen wrench remove the (4) Teflon tranfer tube nipples from the pump body. Using a plastic pick, remove the old Teflon tape from the threads of all (4) transfer tubes. Remove the black exhaust screen gauze and discard the gauze from both quick exhaust ports. Remove the Quick Exhaust port caps and seal. Set the quick exhaust port caps aside for cleaning.

record.field:
Disassembly - Toxic Exh.
Prepare to disassemble pump. Don PPE applicable for working with HF. Remove the 3/8" air supply lines connected to the "SUPY A" and "SUPY B" fittiings. Remove vacuum hose adapters from pump IN port of pump. Save Trebor test fitting thin Teflon gaskets, pn AM082 from the IN and OUT ports. Lift pump off the TPTS grate and place pump on a clean plastic sheet on the work table surface. Remove the plastic male connectors from the base "SUPLY A" and "SUPL B port"s.
Using finger pressure loosen the (4) transfer tube black nut fittings evenly to remove the black base from the Trebor pump. If fittings are too tight use an 15/16" open end wrench or an adjustable wrench to loosen the transfer tube plastic black fittings. The tranfer tube nipples are PFA Teflon and the black nuts and ferrules are polyproplene. Loosen all (4) nuts evenly, then separate the black pump base from the main Trebor pump body. Each transfer tube assembly will have a split ferrule (back) and a ring ferrule (front). Do not loose them, and set aside for cleaning.
Using a clean 1/4 SST Allen wrench remove the (4) Teflon tranfer tube nipples from the pump body. Using a plastic pick, remove the old Teflon tape from the threads of all (4) transfer tubes. Set the transfer aside with the ferrules and nut for cleaning.
Using the exhaust special spanner pin wrench, loosen the muffler base exhaust caps. Remove the black exhaust screen gauze and discard the gauze from both quick exhaust ports. Remove the Quick Exhaust port caps and seal. Set the quick exhaust port caps aside for cleaning.

field.name: STEP_TEXT
field.value: <<bb>>Disassembly - Toxic Exh. <</bb>> <<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>><<nl/>>Remove Trebor Pump Nuts.<<nl/>><<nl/>> Place the Trebor plastic pump adapter pins into the IN and OUT pump ports and finger tighten until the flange rests against the pump body. Lift the pump body and place into the TPST disassembly fixture on the side table disassembly turret shelf. Align the pump pins into the base plastic holes and lock the valve body into place by sliding the pump body. Place the plastic coated aluminum support brace over the pump body and bring up the long all thread studs into the end forks on the aluminum support base. Hand ighten the two all thread knobs to secure the pump body to the disassembly turret fixture. <<nl/>><<nl/>>Using the aluminum spanner wrench, place it over the outside pump union nut. Ensure the lower knob stud is tight to prevent the pump from spinning on the turret mounting fixture. Grasp both wrench handle rods and apply even torque in a counter-clockwise rotation relative to the pump body to loosen the pump union nut. The pumps are assembled with approx. 75 ft-lbs of torque. Unscrew the nut and place it on the table. Remove the pump head cap by gently tapping around the pump head cap to loosen it from the Teflon diaphragm and set aside.<<nl/>><<nl/>> Remove the lowersheft turret locking stud knob stud to enable the pump to swing a complete turn so the other opposite large pump union nut can be removed. Swing the pump body over the pump station and rermove the other union nut. Both union nuts have right hand threads. Remove the nut. Remove the other pump head cap by gently tapping around the pump head to loosen it from the Teflon diaphragm and valve body and set aside.

record.field:
Disassembly - Toxic Exh.
Remove Trebor Pump Nuts.
Place the Trebor plastic pump adapter pins into the IN and OUT pump ports and finger tighten until the flange rests against the pump body. Lift the pump body and place into the TPST disassembly fixture on the side table disassembly turret shelf. Align the pump pins into the base plastic holes and lock the valve body into place by sliding the pump body. Place the plastic coated aluminum support brace over the pump body and bring up the long all thread studs into the end forks on the aluminum support base. Hand ighten the two all thread knobs to secure the pump body to the disassembly turret fixture.
Using the aluminum spanner wrench, place it over the outside pump union nut. Ensure the lower knob stud is tight to prevent the pump from spinning on the turret mounting fixture. Grasp both wrench handle rods and apply even torque in a counter-clockwise rotation relative to the pump body to loosen the pump union nut. The pumps are assembled with approx. 75 ft-lbs of torque. Unscrew the nut and place it on the table. Remove the pump head cap by gently tapping around the pump head cap to loosen it from the Teflon diaphragm and set aside.
Remove the lowersheft turret locking stud knob stud to enable the pump to swing a complete turn so the other opposite large pump union nut can be removed. Swing the pump body over the pump station and rermove the other union nut. Both union nuts have right hand threads. Remove the nut. Remove the other pump head cap by gently tapping around the pump head to loosen it from the Teflon diaphragm and valve body and set aside.

record.field:
Disassembly - Toxic Exh.
Remove the Push Plate and shaft.
Push the round push plate so the other push plate sticks out the pump body. Carefully in a counter-clockwise direction, unscrew and remove the push plate from the main pump shaft. The main shaft is threaded on both ends into a blind tapped hole in the push plate. This hole and threads on the shaft will contain the hazardous fluid that the pump pumped in service. Using the spray rinse- wash out the trapped fluid from the push plate tapped hole and from the main shaft threads. Push out the main shaft and remove it from the valve pump body. Remove the opposite push plate and rinse out its shaft thread and blind tapped hole. Set the main shaft and (2) push plates aside.
Using an X-ACTO knife or a soft O-ring pick tool - CAREFULLY remove the two shaft seals from the main Teflon valve body that the main shaft slides across. Use the sharp point of the X-ACTO blade to carefull pierce the seal. Do not pierce the pick or blade too deep. The valve body must not be damaged. Discard the seals. The seals are PTFE and look similar to piston rings with beveled ends at the gap.
Leave in the main valve body check valve ball components in the IN and OUT PORTS. The body plugs and check ball components are not to be replaced. The disassembly of the pump body is limited to removing the push plates, the shaft and shaft seals.
Remove the Trebor pump base mounting fittings from the IN and OUT ports
The pump components & valve parts can now be cleaned. Do not mix pump components from different pumps. Gather up the pump parts to be cleaned.

Using the spray rinse- wash out the trapped fluid from the push plate tapped hole and from the main shaft threads. Push out the main shaft and remove it from the valve pump body. Remove the opposite push plate and rinse out its shaft thread and blind tapped hole. Set the main shaft and (2) push plates aside.
Using an X-ACTO knife or a soft O-ring pick tool - CAREFULLY remove the two shaft seals from the main Teflon valve body that the main shaft slides across. Use the sharp point of the X-ACTO blade to carefull pierce the seal. Do not pierce the pick or blade too deep. The valve body must not be damaged. Discard the seals. The seals are PTFE and look similar to piston rings with beveled ends at the gap.
Leave in the main valve body check valve ball components in the IN and OUT PORTS. The body plugs and check ball components are not to be replaced. The disassembly of the pump body is limited to removing the push plates, the shaft and shaft seals.
Remove the Trebor pump base mounting fittings from the IN and OUT ports
The pump components & valve parts can now be cleaned. Do not mix pump components from different pumps. Gather up the pump parts to be cleaned.
